audit.title: CCIP Test Tokens - Faucets for EVM and Solana
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured how-to page for minting CCIP test tokens on EVM and Solana testnets, with a strong comparison table for CCIP-BnM vs CCIP-LnM and concrete rate-limit facts. Its single biggest strength is scannability — flat heading hierarchy, no section over 600 words, one crisp token-comparison table. Its biggest opportunity is discoverability: with no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and concept-titled (not symptom-titled) headings, the page is harder for engines to parse and to retrieve on the symptom queries developers actually type. Honest verdict: solid content that will lose retrieval races it should win.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased headings
recommendations.where: section headings throughout (`Quick Start`, `About CCIP Test Tokens`, `LINK Token Faucets`)
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("About CCIP Test Tokens", "General Process").
recommendations.change: add question-form H3s that mirror real queries: "How do I get CCIP-BnM test tokens on Sepolia?", "How do I mint test tokens on Solana Devnet?", "Where do I get LINK for CCIP fees?", "Why is my drip/mint failing?"
recommendations.why: engines retrieve on the query string; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: measured — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)", "canonical: MISSING", dates absent from schema.
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-08-19`, `inLanguage`, and a `<link rel="canonical">` to the non-`.md` URL.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-trust and citation rate; the body already has the date — expose it machine-readably.

recommendations.title: Make the EVM Quick Start chunk self-contained
recommendations.issue: "Call the `drip` function directly on token contracts using the interface below."
recommendations.change: lead with the full answer: name that addresses come from the CCIP Directory, state the mint amount (1 CCIP-BnM = `1e18`), and link the Directory in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: a lifted chunk must stand alone; today it depends on context "below" and elsewhere.

recommendations.title: Quantify EVM mint amount and per-token limits
recommendations.where: "Block Explorer Method" and the token table
recommendations.issue: EVM `drip` mints `1e18` but prose never states "1 token"; Solana limit hedged as "about once every 3 hours".
recommendations.change: state "each EVM `drip` call mints 1 token (1e18 wei)"; if the Solana cadence is exactly 3 hours, drop "about".
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes; vague quantifiers underperform.

recommendations.title: Add a short troubleshooting/FAQ section
recommendations.issue: no coverage of failure modes beyond CAUTION callouts.
recommendations.change: add Q&A entries: "drip reverts / no tokens received", "rate limit — how long to wait", "token not showing in wallet" (link the existing MetaMask import guide), "wallet can't switch to testnet".
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by symptom/error; these sections capture retrieval that prose misses.

recommendations.title: Link one primary/canonical CCIP concept source
recommendations.change: link "cross-chain testing"/burn-and-mint terms to the canonical CCIP architecture/concepts page.
recommendations.why: inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier: "rate‑limited to about once every 3 hours per wallet" — replace with the exact cadence if known.

Code snippet missing context: the Solidity `drip` block shows no imports or contract scope (measured: 1 of 1 block needing imports shows none) — acceptable as an interface excerpt, but label it as such.
No stale content or keyword stuffing detected; date is present and recent.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD may be injected site-wide at the template level; verify with raw `<head>` (not captured here) before treating as a per-page absence.
Freshness cadence: the 2025-08-19 date should be surfaced as `dateModified` schema site-wide, not only in body text.
